title: Ukraine says it downed jet drone with laser for first time
html:

KYIV - Ukraine said it used a laser to shoot down a jet-powered drone for the first time, marking a technological breakthrough in its efforts to repel Russian air attacks.

A “Blysk” laser system installed to protect a critical infrastructure facility downed a Geran drone, Serhii Beskrestnov, defence tech advisor to President Volodymyr Zelensky, said on Telegram on Nov 25, calling the strike a world first.

Lasers “are demonstrating their first results in combat conditions,” though it’s still too early to talk about mass production, he said. “Tests are currently underway, during which lasers are being used to protect critical infrastructure.”

Russia’s jet drones, deployed at scale in 2026, have pounded Ukrainian cities in recent months as their higher speed and mobility make them difficult to intercept with other unmanned aircraft.

Ukraine’s use of lasers is the latest example of innovation by its defence industry in response to Russia’s full-scale invasion, helping to transform modern warfare in ways that Kyiv’s NATO allies are now seeking to emulate.

Israel’s Defence Ministry said last year that it used directed-energy laser systems to deflect “scores” of aerial attacks, including by fixed-wing drones.

Multiple Ukrainian companies are developing laser air defence with the government’s support, Beskrestnov said. Such systems target beams at one part of the drone until its internal components overheat and malfunction.

Russia has escalated strikes on civilian, logistics and energy infrastructure in recent weeks in the run-up to winter, aiming to break Ukrainian morale to impose a settlement favourable to Moscow.

“Russia’s tactics remain unchanged: they target power lines and grids, substations – all to make it harder to transmit electricity from generation facilities,” Zelensky said in a video address late on Nov 25. BLOOMBERG
summary: A “Blysk” laser system installed to protect a critical infrastructure facility downed a Geran drone. Read more at straitstimes.com.
